<details><summary>AI review</summary>

Reviewed at a6097003, together with wpt#63708 at 6d1f7668. The change is correct and minimal. Only the Fragment scripting mode is affected; document parsing, `document.write()` and Inert/Disabled parsing still set *force async* to false. The tests cover:
- `createContextualFragment()`;
- the six `*HTMLUnsafe()` methods with `runScripts`, on both connected and disconnected targets, plus `ShadowRoot`;
- the legacy setters with a Trusted Types default policy enabling `runScripts`.

Per spec, a default policy's `createParserOptions` overrides the caller's `runScripts`, so the "policy sets `runScripts: true`" variants are valid for `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML()` and the `*HTMLUnsafe()` methods in the tests.

**Suggestions**
- `source:68343-68345`: the [force async](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#script-force-async) definition still says "It is set to false by the HTML parser and the XML parser on `script` elements they insert". That's no longer true in the Fragment scripting mode. Consider adding "except when the HTML parser's scripting mode is Fragment".
- `source:147051-147054`: the first note paragraph explains that Fragment-mode scripts are treated as not parser-inserted, but not what that now means for their timing. Consider adding: "Their force async stays true, so external scripts without an `async` attribute execute asynchronously once inserted."
- `unsafe-and-trusted-types-external-scripts-async.html:10-23`: because of the page-wide `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` and the default policy's `createParserOptions`, the "`{ runScripts: true }`" subtests (`:91-148`) also get their options from the policy as a `TrustedHTMLParserOptions`. The `SetHTMLUnsafeOptions` dictionary path is never exercised. Consider moving them to a file without the CSP and the policy.
- Both files, `setupEvents()`/`:16-18`: if an assertion fails before the `await`, `slow.js` is still loading. It then pushes `"slow"` into the next subtest's `window.events` and calls that subtest's `on_slow`, so one failure can cascade into the following subtests. Consider tagging each subtest's scripts with its id and ignoring stale ones. For example, `slow.js` could check `new URL(document.currentScript.src).searchParams.get("id")` against the current subtest's id before pushing, and the `data:` script could embed the id the same way.

</details>

> AI review

Addressed suggestions and WPT issues.

<details><summary>AI review</summary>

Reviewed at 9b897a3a, together with web-platform-tests/wpt#63708 at f4018416. The spec side looks good, and lint and the build pass:
- the force async definition now has the Fragment-mode exception;
- the note explains the async consequence;
- the tests are split, so `html-unsafe-external-scripts-async.html` exercises the dictionary path without Trusted Types;
- each subtest's scripts are tagged with its id.

**Blockers**
- wpt `domparsing/resources/slow.js:1`: the top-level `const id` is a global lexical declaration. The second time a page runs `slow.js`, it throws "SyntaxError: Identifier 'id' has already been declared", so `on_slow` is never called. On wpt.fyi PR head (Chrome 158.0.8106), `html-unsafe-external-scripts-async.html` and `unsafe-and-trusted-types-external-scripts-async.html` both end with that harness error. In each, the first subtest passes, the second times out, and the rest don't run. `createContextualFragment-external-scripts-async.html` only loads it once, so it passes. Consider wrapping it in a block:

```js
{
  const id = new URL(document.currentScript.src).searchParams.get('id');
  if (id === String(window.current_test_id)) {
    window.events.push('slow');
    window.on_slow?.();
  }
}
```

</details>

> AI review

Fixed the WPT issue.
